newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan deregulation's good effect not yet clear - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan deregulation's good effect not yet clear - EPA.

text.p: Uncertainties over Japan's economic prospects probably stem from people not yet being able to see the positive effects of deregulation measures, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso told a news conference on Friday.

Aso said: "Even though we are likely to achieve 2.5 percent growth this fiscal year (ending March 31), people say there is not yet positive sentiment about the economy. I think this is due to uncertainties related to economic structural adjustments."
He added that he did not think a rise in the consumption tax in April to five percent from three percent was contributing very much to the uncertainties over economic prospects.

Media reports had said previous falls in Tokyo stock prices were due to the slowness of deregulation being carried out in Japan, but structural reforms including deregulation were steadily progressing, he said.
This could be seen in a bill to reform Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, which was approved by Friday morning's cabinet meeting, he said.

"The positive effects from deregulation measures will not appear until later," Aso said. When people see that deregulation creates new ideas and jobs, they will start noticing the good impact, he said.

Aso said Management and Coordination Agency Minister Kabun Muto will meet individually with some ministers early next week to discuss deregulation measures which the government is planning to finalise by the end of March.
